requirement_text.REQ-405:
P1. Implements 0039 D3's backend check. No new hex dependency.

BUILDS `lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_boundaries.ex` (`mix letflow.check_boundaries`), built on `mix xref graph --format plain` file-level edges. It exits non-zero and prints each offending edge when:
(a) a file outside every `lib/letflow/modules/<id>/` directory references a file inside one, EXCEPT `lib/letflow/modules/catalog.ex`, the one sanctioned importer (D3). The mechanism files directly in `lib/letflow/modules/*.ex` (one level, no subdirectory) are core, not a module (D3).
(b) a file in `lib/letflow/modules/a/` references a file in `lib/letflow/modules/b/` when `b` is not in module `a`'s manifest `depends_on` (read through `Letflow.Modules.Catalog`).

Edge classification is a pure function over the parsed xref output so it can be unit-tested with synthetic edge lists.

SCOPE: only edges whose SOURCE file is under `lib/`. Test code under `test/support/` is excluded.

Add `"letflow.check_boundaries"` to the `"letflow.check"` alias in `mix.exs` after `"compile --warnings-as-errors"`. CI already runs `mix letflow.check`.

Known limit: xref does not see `apply/3` or string-built module names.

OUT OF SCOPE: the frontend ESLint rule (REQ-406).

task.description: Design `mix letflow.check_boundaries` (REQ-405): the xref-based module boundary check wired into `mix letflow.check`. Write `lib/letflow/design/req405-check-boundaries.md` covering the task module structure, the pure `classify_edge/2` function and its 6 classification cases, @spec annotations, mix.exs alias slot and T-ALIAS-SLOT test update, test structure for AC1–AC5, and the no-new-dependency proof. Design only — no implementation code.
acceptance_criteria: Module structure for lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_boundaries.ex specified (run/1, classify_edge/2, parse_xref_output/1, build_depends_on_map/1 with full @spec annotations)
All 5 AC1 edge cases (plus scope exclusion rule) documented in classification table §2.3 with correct :ok / {:violation, reason} verdicts
mix.exs alias insertion slot identified (after compile --warnings-as-errors, before letflow.check.test) with T-ALIAS-SLOT test assertions specified
Test structure documented for AC1 (unit), AC2 (system), AC3 (probe procedure), AC4 (alias wiring), AC5 (no-dep proof)
No implementation code in design doc (signatures and type shapes only)

result.summary: Design complete. Key decisions: (1) `classify_edge/2` is a pure two-argument function taking `{source, target}` and a `depends_on_map` built from `Catalog.all_manifests/0`; scope gate filters out non-lib/ sources and test/support/ sources before classification. (2) Six classification rules in first-match order: Rule 0 (target not in module subdir → OK), Rule 1 (catalog.ex sanctioned importer → OK), Rules 2/3 (intra-module or authorized cross-module → OK), Rule 4 (unauthorized cross-module → VIOLATION), Rule 5 (outsider imports module → VIOLATION). (3) Alias slot: after `compile --warnings-as-errors`, before `letflow.check.test`; T-ALIAS-SLOT test asserts both ordering constraints. (4) No new dependency: `mix xref` is built-in, `System.cmd/3` is stdlib, `Catalog.all_manifests/0` is existing code. (5) AC3 probe procedure documented in §5.4: since no lib/letflow/modules/<id>/ subdir currently exists, ELIXIR-DEV must create a synthetic one plus a caller probe, run the check, then remove both before committing. Open questions: none.
